html:
The Nyawaygi, also spelt Nyawigi, are an Aboriginal Australian people whose country lay around Halifax Bay in north Queensland, near today's Ingham. They may also have lived on Orpheus Island. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Their land runs from mangrove coast and islands up to rainforested ranges. Little is recorded of them; their language was documented by the linguist R. M. W. Dixon from one of its last speakers. Neighbours on the map include the Gugu Badhun, the Warrgamay and the Dyirbal. Sugar cane plantations took over the coastal plain from the 1870s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
